# Copilot Instructions

## Commands
This repository does not commit build, test, or lint tooling. Python dependencies are declared in `pyproject.toml`, and the entry points should still be launched from `src\` because `app.py` starts sibling scripts by bare filename.

```powershell
Set-Location src
python series_context_tool.py <video-or-title> --context-model qwen3.5:9b
python app.py
python process_audio.py <video-file> --pipeline-mode current --asr-source mix --asr-model large-v3
python process_audio.py <video-file> --pipeline-mode balanced --judge-model qwen3.5:9b --context-model qwen3.5:9b
python process_audio.py <video-file> --pipeline-mode max --judge-model qwen3.5:9b --context-model qwen3.5:9b
python process_audio.py <video-file> --asr-source mix --asr-model hybrid
python process_audio.py <video-file> --asr-source mix --asr-model kotoba-whisper-v1.1
python translate_subs.py <json-file> --pipeline-mode current --translation-model qwen3:14b
python translate_subs.py <json-file> --pipeline-mode balanced --translation-model qwen3:14b --judge-model qwen3.5:9b
python translate_subs.py <json-file> --pipeline-mode max --translation-model qwen3:14b --translation-secondary-model translategemma:12b --judge-model qwen3.5:9b
python check_settings.py --pipeline-mode balanced --asr-source mix --asr-model large-v3 --separator-model model_bs_roformer_ep_317_sdr_12.9755.ckpt --translation-model qwen3:14b --translation-secondary-model translategemma:12b --judge-model qwen3.5:9b --context-model qwen3.5:9b
python check_gpu.py
```

`process_audio.py` assumes `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` are available, CUDA-backed `faster-whisper` is available, `stable-ts` is installed for timestamp refinement, and the `audio_separator` model assets can be cached under `.\temp`. On Windows, the code now auto-detects the standard Winget FFmpeg install location even if it is not already on `PATH`. The advanced Kotoba path also depends on the Transformers stack declared in `pyproject.toml`. `translate_subs.py` assumes a local Ollama server at `http://localhost:11434` with the configured model available; the current primary translation default is `qwen3:14b`, while judge/context/secondary-model roles can now be passed explicitly. `series_context_tool.py` can fetch public anime metadata and save normalized `series_context.json` entries into the global app cache. `check_settings.py` is the quick preflight path for the current UI selection, including the intended `onnxruntime-gpu` Windows/Linux setup.

## Architecture
- `app.py` is the CustomTkinter desktop shell. It owns folder selection, queueing, skip/cancel controls, the selected-file count/select-all UI, and the progress/output console. It also owns the advanced processing settings that are passed to the worker scripts as explicit CLI arguments, including the processing profile (`current`, `balanced`, `max`), preset-plus-optional-custom model-role overrides, an optional local `series_context.json` override path, and dedicated **Check Settings** / **Check GPU** buttons that run validation scripts through the same console/progress surface.
- For each selected video, `app.py` runs `process_audio.py` first and then `translate_subs.py` against the generated `<base>.json`. It reads the child process output byte-by-byte so `tqdm` carriage-return updates can drive the GUI progress bar.
- `process_audio.py` is the audio/transcription stage. In `current` mode it preserves the existing single-path behavior. In `balanced` and `max`, it loads reusable series context, transcribes both the mixed track and raw vocals with `large-v3`, collects suspicious/disagreement windows, optionally runs Kotoba on those windows, and can use a judge model to pick the best JP candidate before the final timing pass. The default Whisper path also uses compact title/name hotwords derived from the series context instead of only the filename.
- `translate_subs.py` is the LLM translation/export stage. In `current` mode it keeps the existing deterministic single-model flow. In `balanced` and `max`, it can add a judge/normalizer pass and, for `max`, a secondary translation candidate before the final merged/display export. It reads the same series context used by the JP stage, caches the translated JSON with profile/model/context hashes, repairs fragmentary multi-cue windows, and writes `.jp.srt`, `.romaji.srt`, `.en.raw.srt`, and a merged/display-formatted `.en.srt`.
- `series_context_tool.py` is the shared context-fetch utility. It can infer the series title from a filename, look up public anime metadata, optionally normalize it with a local Ollama model, and persist the result into the global cache for future runs.
- `check_settings.py` validates the active UI settings without processing a file. It checks FFmpeg, Python modules, ONNX provider visibility, Ollama reachability/model names, the selected separator checkpoint, and the optional `series_context.json` override.
- `check_gpu.py` is a diagnostics-only script for CUDA/provider readiness across PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, and `faster-whisper`.

## Key conventions
- Cache files control reruns. If `<base>.json` already exists and its `meta.timing_refinement_version` matches the current code, `process_audio.py` skips work and just re-exports the SRTs. Older JSON caches are treated as upgradeable transcripts only when the selected transcription source, ASR model, pipeline mode, inferred series title, series-context hash, transcription prompt version, judge model, and relevant separator checkpoint still match; otherwise the script intentionally regenerates the Japanese transcript. If `<base>_translated.json` exists, `translate_subs.py` skips Ollama calls only when the Japanese transcript text, inferred series title, series-context hash, pipeline mode, selected model-role settings, and translation prompt version still match; otherwise it regenerates the translated cache on purpose so English wording does not drift against the current configuration. The reusable global `series_context.json` cache lives outside the repo under the OS cache directory.
- Output files are written next to the source video or JSON, but intermediate vocal stems and normalized WAV files live under `.\temp` relative to the current working directory.
- `.gitattributes` enforces LF line endings for text files in the repository. Preserve LF when editing or adding tracked text files, even when working from Windows.
- `app.py` now parses worker JSON status lines into human-readable GUI status updates while still watching percentage-bearing `tqdm` output to drive the progress bar. If you change logging, keep the `%`-bearing `tqdm` output intact and keep JSON status payloads machine-readable so the GUI can distinguish in-progress phases from true completion.
- The transcription defaults are intentionally tuned for Japanese anime, not general speech: `--asr-source mix`, `--asr-model large-v3`, `language="ja"`, `condition_on_previous_text=False`, VAD enabled with tighter silence/padding thresholds, and `word_timestamps=False`. The default/current path also front-loads the inferred or cached series title into Whisper's initial prompt and hotwords to reduce proper-noun/title drift without re-enabling previous-text conditioning. `balanced` and `max` use dual-source review (`mix` + `raw_vocals`) plus targeted rescue windows instead of trusting one source. `normalized_vocals` remains a legacy option, not the default, because recent A/B work showed it can hurt subtitle coverage. `kotoba-whisper-v1.1` is available as an advanced option but still merges cues more aggressively than the stable current path.
- Hybrid suspicious-window collection is deliberately narrow: it starts from the refined Whisper baseline, expands around suspicious seed cues (ASCII-heavy output, repeated-noise style text, or the existing long sparse cue heuristic), adds selected long-gap rescue windows, and only accepts Kotoba replacements that pass the current score/count/duration safeguards. Keep that behavior targeted; do not silently turn hybrid into a full second-pass rewrite of the whole episode.
- The translation step has two prompt modes. General chat models still use the 1:1 JSON-list batch prompt with previous/next subtitle context. Translation-specialist models like `translategemma:12b` instead use direct per-line subtitle prompts plus series-context blocks so they do not accidentally translate the surrounding context. `qwen3:14b` remains the incumbent primary translator; `qwen3.5:9b` is the default judge/context model; `translategemma:12b` is the default secondary candidate in `max`.
- English subtitle export has two modes: `.en.raw.srt` preserves the original segment timing 1:1, while `.en.srt` can merge repaired fragment windows into viewer-facing cues and then split oversized English subtitles back into timed chunks capped at two on-screen lines.
